title: Spike: choose IPLD codec for article root node (DAG-CBOR vs DAG-JSON)
description:
Choose the IPLD codec for the usenet-ipfs article root node. The two candidates are DAG-CBOR (0x71) and DAG-JSON (0x0129). Different codecs produce different CIDs for the same logical content, so this choice is permanent once articles are written to IPFS and referenced in group logs.

Key constraint: Corundum uses DAG-JSON for its MVP content objects. Corundum plans to add an rfc822+mime activity type whose content reference CID points at a usenet-ipfs article root node. If usenet-ipfs uses DAG-CBOR and Corundum uses DAG-JSON, the CIDs are different and Corundum cannot reference the canonical usenet-ipfs article CID directly — it would have to wrap or re-encode.

Evaluate: (1) DAG-CBOR: more compact, standard for storage-optimized IPLD, but different CID from DAG-JSON. (2) DAG-JSON: human-readable, same codec as Corundum MVP, enables direct CID cross-referencing. (3) Whether Corundum's future codec upgrade path matters here.

Artifact: decision recorded in issue notes; CLAUDE.md updated; l62.2.9.1 (schema) and l62.2.9.8 (root node builder) updated to reflect chosen codec.
notes: DECISION: DAG-CBOR (codec 0x71). Rationale: (1) More compact than DAG-JSON — better for storage and bandwidth. (2) Standard for IPFS/IPLD storage — most IPFS implementations default to DAG-CBOR. (3) Corundum can reference DAG-CBOR CIDs from its DAG-JSON activities — the codec of referenced content need not match the referencing document. (4) Corundum's future upgrade path from DAG-JSON to DAG-CBOR would align both systems. Corundum consultation: Corundum stores content references as CID bytes in its own DAG-JSON; the referenced content codec is transparent to the referencing layer. Implementation: serde_ipld_dagcbor 0.6. IRREVERSIBLE once articles are written to IPFS. CLAUDE.md updated.
